pitch_detail.notes: Crack leading left to a pine around 30 ft up, then twin hand cracks that taper into a single finger crack by a large bush. Ends on a ledge with a rappel anchor. Solid climbing.

Thin crack above the belay meets a wider one 20 ft up. Move right of the bush into a flare of hand and fist jams to a ledge. Then follow the arete, mixing small cams, nuts and bolts, to a bushy headwall and the last bolt, and go right to a big ledge. A short #4-size crack and a dihedral finish it. Needs a 70 m rope. A bit dirty with lichen and brush.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches with grades and lengths (115 ft, 200 ft converted). Rappel is by tree anchors west of a neighbouring route, not a station list, so no rappel table. Bolts on P2 stated only as 4 total in the protection line, left off the pitch field.

pitch_detail.notes: Begin beside the neighbouring route and angle into the dihedral to its left, then work the crack straight toward the shrubs and push through them. The central stretch protects poorly, hence the PG13 tag: expect a runout, with a sling on a manzanita for pro. A few short passages of good hand jams follow. Top out on a sloping manzanita flat at a stout tree. A loose flake sits about 35 ft up.

Go roughly 20 ft ahead to the wall, then head for a crack system up and left. Get into the crack, exit left about 20 ft up to avoid loose flakes near a small tree, traverse back right into it, and climb it up and rightward. Loose blocks at the top threaten the belayer.

rappel_detail.station: pine in the gully west of the route, about 100 ft west of the top and 20 ft down
rappel_detail.notes: Roping up for the approach is wise. No webbing on the trees; loop the rope around the trunk, it retrieves easily.

rappel_detail.station: ledge with a pine on its west edge
rappel_detail.notes: Lands on a walk-off into the main gully.

review.changed: Wrote two pitches; P1 length 160 ft converted, P2 length left out (85 with no unit). Pitch grades not stated, so none written. Wrote two rappels (35 m each) listed in the descent.
review.other_findings: Loose flake (P1) and loose blocks (top of P2) noted as hazards awaiting trundling.

pitch_detail.notes: Blocky fourth-class to easy fifth-class terrain up to the foot of the prominent pitch 2 corner. Perhaps about 5.5, but that is only a guess. Gear belay.
Dihedral climbed by stemming, mantling and the odd jam. Gear is available throughout, though mostly in cracks beside the corner. Reserve a #3 for the top belay, then walk off.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches; no pitch grades stated for P2 and P1 is a hedged guess so it is in notes only. No lengths stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Leads to the main part of the route. Bolt protected.

Two distinct cruxes. One arrives early past a small roof: technical edging on a steep, unusual slab that ends sooner than expected. The middle is much easier but still engaging, and the second hard section sits high where the wall steepens. Bolt protected.

review.changed: Wrote two pitches; text gives little detail on P1. No lengths, bolt counts or anchors stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Wide chimney, squeezing past two big chockstones on the right. Belay at the bolts on the right.
Narrow slot up to the top, where a solid gear anchor can be built just short of the finish. This slot is the reason to climb the route, and only when it holds snow.
Short, with a few awkward moves to the summit area. Can be run together with pitch 2, but splitting them may work better.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches. Descent is the South Gully, no rappels.

pitch_detail.notes: Terraced third-class ground leads to an alcove where the real climbing starts. A bouldery start gives onto a 5.6 slab tilting right, then a steep fist crack. Work left via fluted right-facing corners to a pulpit and roomy alcove belay that accepts hand-size gear.

Nicknamed the crystal cave pitch. Fingers in the alcove's left side, then a leftward face traverse to a jam, up through a crystal cave and over a roof. Above, climb the front of a large block (a #1 fits in the right-hand crack) or lieback its left edge, then traverse its top by hand. A 5 inch offwidth splitter ends at a sloping-ledge belay.

Nicknamed the bighorn splitter. Weave up blocks to the splitter right over the belay, climb the finger crack through a roof into tight hands. A horizontal dike partway up holds the crux, a finger-and-face sequence protected by a wire and cams below. Past it, bear-hug hand jams and further splitter lead to a terrace belay.

Uses the full rope. Start left of centre on the terrace: steep fingers-to-hands splitter, more cracks, a left-facing corner, then left into a steep hand crack and an awkward topout over blocks. Fourth class heads toward the last steep step, where a flared 5.10c finger crack with sparse gear (a #3 in a pod, micros) guards the one-bolt belay beneath the orange headwall. Much rope is out at the crux, so split it if unsure.

Called the Lien Pitch. Go up and left over unprotected 5.9 face to a right-slanting crack, whose first piece is a bomber #.4. Pass a pod taking a 3 inch cam, then climb face to the obvious crack. Fun 5.11a moves precede the crux: flared thin jams and face around a subtle bulge, then a strenuous flared crack to the belay.

Technical face from the belay gives way to excellent cracks trending right via knobs and plates. About 20 ft under the ridge a horizontal break offers a rest, then a vertical crack and face finish gain the ridge. After bringing your second up, scramble easy fifth class toward the summit.

review.changed: Wrote all six pitches; stated lengths on P1, P2, P4, P5 only. Text gives plain .10, read as 5.10. No rappel table; descent is a walk-off east toward Mt Pickering.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble the large right-facing corner near mid-mountain, switch to a smaller one ending in a thin hand crack, then bear right at the ledge and follow flakes to a good ledge. Step right to the bolted anchor.

Take the groove to the right, step right across blocky features and aim for the foot of the huge dihedral that forms the base of a heart-shaped feature under big roofs. Cracks on its left side lead to a small ledge.
Steep splitters, stemming and jamming, to an alcove below large roofs. A wild mantle onto a diving-board flake ends the pitch, with the belay on top.

Steep corner with overhangs, then a long crack in fingers and hands with the occasional fist, becoming offwidth for a few moves right below Throne Room Ledge. A #4 was the largest cam used, though bigger might feel better.

review.changed: Wrote the four pitches the text gives per-pitch. Above Throne Room Ledge the text only lists options (straight up the splitter, or left to easier ground and across to join another route), so no further pitches written.
review.other_findings: Row says 8 pitches; text details only 4, with open finish options above.

pitch_detail.notes: Stemming and jamming cracks, a short wide pod, hand cracks to a ledge system, then an easier wide corner to a ledge.

Wide bulges in a large right-facing corner, finishing in a short hand-crack corner. If big cams are left behind, expect 5.7 offwidth above a #4. At the top, step left, delicately and in the air, into a hand crack over a small flake visible from below, and follow it to a rock pile beneath an orange iron band.

Stem through a brief wide section (protectable) in the iron band to an exposed hand crack and face, then paired hand cracks to a well-protected small roof. Over it, fifth-class blocks and a 5.6 step left lead to a nest belay by a big horn.
Crawl behind the horn, downclimb slightly, then go up steep blocks to a ridge and along it to an exposed sloping block belay under the last arete block. A 70 m rope helps here.

Pass the arete block's roof on the right, up brief hollow flakes to firmer cracks. Put a cam in a horizontal, then exposed 5.7 R arete ends at a large sandy ledge. Down and right, a third-class gully reaches the summit plateau.

review.changed: Wrote all five pitches. Route has no fixed protection.

pitch_detail.notes: Begins where blocks form a bulge like an arete on the buttress's lower right toe. Cracks past a bush lead to blockier ground and, by the easiest way, to an alcove belay at the left.
Exit the alcove any way you like and target a left-facing corner holding a hand crack. It ends at a smooth ledge in a big white granite corner. Belay under the thin Y crack.

Y crack: balance and thin gear, with one piton where it pinches out. A hand-crack bulge brings you to the face, then a leftward move of about 5 m. Choose the lower footrail with no gear to a corner system, or go up to a tiny ledge system and move left with gear, which means a harder, more delicate step into the corner. The easier-looking lower line, though runout, may be the better choice. Corner system ends at a stance below the crack through the orange band.

Possibly 5.10b. Good jams through the iron band, then trickier above the first bulge with thin gear and delicate face. A right-facing corner has thin opening moves, a bold move past another bulge, and a hand crack follows until it stops. Step right to the arete and a blocky belay perch.
Follow the arete to a small pinnacle, sticking to the crest for added cracks and exposure. Down from the pinnacle, the fifth-class ridge continues; climb as far as the rope reaches.

Right of a small roof under the last slabs, through grainy corners and loose-feeling flakes to a sharp arete. The bold finish: cam in a horizontal at foot level, then runout exposed 5.7 arete to the summit block.

Jam and stem past the opening roof, then enjoy crack and face moves with good gear. Near the top a brief awkward wide flare calls for a #4. Bolts at around 130 ft; alternatively skip the last section and traverse right to lower from the next route's anchor. Still somewhat dirty.
Further pitch at 5.9, finishing at a tree anchor.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. P1 has no stated grade, left blank; length is approximate (about 130 ft) so kept in notes.

pitch_detail.notes: From the formation's lowest toe, drift right over easy ramps with one short vertical bit to a roomy ledge below a vertical-to-overhanging wall. Belay by the left-leaning crack that cuts it.

Vertical to overhanging crack tracking well left, with smearing feet. Width goes from thin hands (about #.75) to small fist pods. Treat the grade as approximate; it was estimated while cleaning flakes. Belay in decent cracks to the right once it eases, on hand-size cams.

Over 30 m. Leave the belay going left to an easier hand crack skirting a blank shield's left side. Belay on the first ledge (about 15 m) to spare rope drag, or continue 15 m more along the left-trending cracks to the formation's left edge.
Between 5.8 and 5.9. Stay just left of the east-northeast ridge in a gully-like zone full of crack choices. Belay close to the summit ridge.
Arete to the top. Reasonable gear if you search for it.

review.changed: Wrote all six pitches, with pitches 3 and 4 as one linked entry as the text treats them. Descent is a gully walk-off, no rappels.

pitch_detail.notes: Wide crack of moderate difficulty steepens into fingers and hands, 150+ ft up to a flat ledge. Belay with 2 to 3 inch cams.
Steep finger and hand crack, easy for its angle, 150+ ft to the top. Set a gear belay, or continue back to the bolted anchor of the adjacent route.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. Rappel is two raps on one 70 m rope down the neighbouring route, described as a general rope-length note rather than a station list, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Begin on the left of the first rocky ledge, left of where Mindy starts and beneath the right half of the first huge roof. Blocky stemming and jamming over some bulges reaches twin wide cracks, which lead to a big ledge. Belay on its left.
Obvious hand crack, then around the roof's left side, more hands, and right to a fine ledge below a giant roof.

Crack system through roofs: go over the roof at right, then one crack, mostly hands, to a huge ledge. Many perfect ledges allow splitting into two 5.9 leads. For a single lead, triples of .75 to #2 are handy.
Hand crack in the headwall's right side, then delicate face where it fades. Step left onto a ledge, climb twin cracks up the face centre to the ridge, and belay.

rappel_detail.station: on the ridge about 15 ft south of the top
rappel_detail.notes: Down and to skier's right toward a station beneath a small overhang. Carry extra tat in case the cord is worn.
Straight down, drifting a little skier's left, to a station under a big overhang (the third you pass).
Down and slightly skier's left to a station set on a low-angle slab.
Final drop reaches the wall's foot; scramble skier's left to the packs. Length not stated.

review.changed: Wrote four pitches and four rappels in order; the last rappel length is not stated. Walk-off option is in the stored descent.
review.other_findings: Row grade is 5.10- but no pitch is graded above 5.9+.

pitch_detail.notes: Easy blocks to a wide ledge. Take the flared black finger crack (5.10b), or the simpler tight hands crack in the dihedral on its left, to the next ledge. Belay under a finger crack that cuts a bulge above.

Climb horns and blocks to a ledge holding a big bush, skirt it, and go up the overhanging finger crack by laybacking or jamming past the roof to more fingers. Belay on a small left-hand stance, on a splitter taking a #.75 or #1. Joining pitch 1 works if you use the 5.10b crack, but drag is nasty.

A tight hands crack leads into the first of three roofs, which widen from hands to fists. Over the last one, continue to a large ledge. Alternate start, no #4 needed: stay on the splitter you belay from and use jugs and crimps for a mildly spicy step right into the main line.
Up flared, scruffy, intermittent cracks to a slim ledge, wrap right through a brief lieback to a triangular roof, then left to a comfortable ledge. Slings and back-cleaning can link it to pitch 5.
Steep golden hands splitter, then interesting features, to a wide ledge.

Shift the belay up and left to under the weak line through the middle of the upper headwall. Intermittent cracks and holds, with generous gear. Exit roughly 10 ft right of the first rappel stones; slings there are not guaranteed.

rappel_detail.station: on the ridge about 10 ft south of the top (bring cord)
rappel_detail.notes: Go down and skier's right to a station beneath a small overhang. The distance is exactly 35 m.
Straight down, bearing a little skier's left, to a station under a big overhang (the third you cross).
Down and slightly right to a station on a low-angle slab.
Last drop lands at the base; scramble skier's left for your gear. Length not stated.

review.changed: Wrote six pitches and four rappels in order.

pitch_detail.notes: Jugs in a wide crack system lead to a right-facing dihedral with tight hands, up to the next big ledge. Either stop there or climb the following right-facing dihedral to a stance beneath the offwidth.

Finger crack in a left-facing dihedral, then stem and jam over into the wide crack on the right wall (#4 and #5 territory). Jam and layback past the overhang to better features, go left around the roof as on the neighbouring route, and follow a finger crack to a ledge. A left-facing dihedral with many cracks ends at the ledge under that route's roof pitch. From there carry on up it, or step right 10 to 15 ft toward another route's third pitch.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. No rappel table: the rappel descent in the text belongs to the top-out of neighbouring routes.

pitch_detail.notes: Crack system over a string of bulges (jam, stem, layback) to the roomy ledge under a hands-to-fist crack.
Hand-to-fist crack to the roof, then left. More cracks reach a ledge, followed by triple cracks in a left-facing dihedral to a ledge below the big-roofed right-facing dihedral. Belay.
Finger crack to a roof, which you pull in tips to fingers: the crux. Higher, struggle up a bulging fist crack to a massive ledge.

Twin hand cracks on the ledge's left, over blocks. Where they stop, get onto a small sandy ledge and avoid the chossy chimney by moving up-left along the arete to a narrow ledge, then twin cracks with nice face moves to the ridge.

rappel_detail.station: on the ridge about 15 ft south of the top
rappel_detail.notes: Down and to skier's right toward a station beneath a small overhang. Carry extra tat in case the cord is worn.
Straight down, drifting a little skier's left, to a station under a big overhang (the third you pass).
Down and slightly right to a station set on a low-angle slab.
Final drop reaches the base. Length not stated.

review.changed: Wrote four pitches and four rappels in order.
review.other_findings: Row grade 5.10b, but P3 is graded 5.10c.

pitch_detail.notes: Chimney in three dimensions, then delicate gear-protected slab to a small perch beneath a huge flake jutting from the corner.
Corner facing left: a thin seam that widens to hands and ends steep and wide. Ledge belay on a slung horn. Link with pitch 1 if you can.
All steep, sustained fingers to hands up to a large ledge. Continue along the corner system, via a chimney, to another big ledge with a giant leaning block.

Skip the chimney straight ahead; jam the hands corner (left-facing) just right of it, pull a small roof and reach airy slabs. Cracks angle up-left to the ridge. Alternative: bear right past the roof into a steep crack to the ridge.
Scrambling on the blocky ridge, with a 10 ft downclimb left around a cube-shaped gendarme. Hollow blocks guard the Orange Pillar's twin splitters; a burly roof traverse reaches the belay ledge.

Right-hand splitter on the Orange Pillar, sustained at 1 to 1.5 inches, then an insecure move right into a wide chimney. Climb the chimney with no gear (5.7 R, footholds are good), exit right onto easy face with gear in horizontals.
Brief steep hand crack into a notch, down by climbing or rappel. No fixed anchor exists; footholds beside the crack make downclimbing practical. Also rated A0.

Walk the ridge to where it forces a 15 ft traverse right across doubtful flakes, then a fierce, well-protected, dirty mantel. Or take the dirty steep hands-to-fists crack left of it. Pass a baby-sized xenolith to an alcove belay.
Acute corners in a row, then blockier cracks and a last mantel onto the ridge, where you belay.
Walk the thin ridge to an offwidth made by an enormous detached flake; a single bolt covers it. Walk on and belay under the 3 inch splitter at a two-bolt anchor.
Steep hands-and-fists splitter over a roof, an offwidth through a second roof, then a bold finish on big features. Two bolts; bring a #4 (a #5 is optional).

review.changed: Wrote all eleven pitches; feet converted to metres. No rappel table; descent is over the summit of Mount Crocker and down its west ridge.

pitch_detail.notes: Graded 5.10d or 5.11a, 20 to 25 m. Starting above the snowfield, a thin crack on a big semi-detached block's left side (5.9); if the base is wet, use the block's right. Left past a bolt into a flared crack of fingers to thin hands (5.10a), then left over the slab with three bolts, the crux, to a two-bolt stance.

Graded 5.10, 50 to 55 m. Cam high in the crack before going left; two xenoliths serve as footholds, then lean over to a flake. A 1-2 inch splitter takes jams for about 50 ft to steep flakes, then left past a bolt on black knobs (5.9) to a bolted stance. Hold back a #2 and #3 for the upper crack. With a 70 m rope, climb past the bolts to a ledge and build an anchor with a #4 held back.

50 to 55 m. Left, then a hand crack (5.8) through a short 3-4 inch section to a large ledge. Staircase terrain by the easiest line meets a neighbouring route, whose 15 ft finger crack (5.10a) guards a ledge with a bolted anchor.

Graded 5.10 or 5.11. Strenuous 4 inch splitter, four bolts so a 4 inch cam can be bumped up it. Roof, mantle, then left to a bolted offwidth. Carry a few finger-size pieces for the upper offwidth and chimney.
60 to 70 m of easy scrambling over very loose blocks, trending up and right to the foot of an orange 1-1.5 inch left-facing corner on the buttress's right side.

Graded 5.10a to 5.10c, 45 to 50 m. The orange corner begins at 1-1.5 inches and opens to 2-3. It runs up and right to a large ledge, where a 5.10c right-leaning crack reaches the belay ledge. Or belay on the lower ledge and traverse right.
About 35 m. Around the corner to the right, then blocky ground and two easy twin cracks; tuck under a huge overhang to an anchor at a roomy ledge.
About 35 m, some 5.10. Scramble along the ridge to a short offwidth with bolts: a boulder problem to a big jug that can feel hard, especially if you are short.
Graded 5.10d or 5.11a, depending on hand size. Steep hands to fists over a large roof and on to a second; the upper section eases but stays steep. Two neighbouring routes also end here.

review.changed: Wrote all nine pitches; where the text gives ranges or two grades they are in the notes, not fields. No rappel table (descent options unfinished).

skip_reasons.ca_long_buttress_devil_s_snare: Text describes only a single-pitch variation to the first pitch of Magic Staircase, not a pitch-by-pitch breakdown of a two-pitch route.
skip_reasons.ca_mount_whitney_inyo_face: Text covers only part of the route: first two pitches were off-route, upper pitches unknown, and the pitch count (10) cannot be matched.
